attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter, endorsed.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps his three points: 'powerful' is a marketing term, the media doesn't understand what it describes, and 'agent' has been stretched to cover any LLM. It also keeps 'at this point'. The language is very sweeping, but it is a firm present-tense observation.

contract.note: Reading 'any' as rhetorical breadth rather than a literal universal is fair and ordinary. Requiring evidence of a widespread pattern and of a lack of understanding matches his words. The May 2025 window was chosen by the evaluator but is reasonable for an ongoing observation.

evidence.note: CIO piece from April 2025, before the target month. It reports agent-washing by vendors but itself examines the term critically. It is one article and says nothing about how common either pattern is.
MacRumors, May 2025. It uses 'most powerful' but also gives benchmark scores and specific capabilities. One isolated example cannot show a widespread pattern or that journalists lack understanding.

reviews.rationale: The packet has no representative coded corpus of May 2025 coverage. The two items cut both ways: some promotional wording, but also critical scrutiny and concrete capability descriptions. Neither shows prevalence or what journalists understand. Under the contract, the claim cannot be settled on this evidence.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter, endorsed.

semantics.note: It is correctly treated as causal: losses already happening and caused by Google's AI summaries. The scope of search-dependent major outlets is kept. Leaving out the social-network clause is appropriate.

contract.note: Reading 'large chunks' as substantial publisher-level traffic loss is fair. The causal-control requirements are demanding, but the contract also accepts reputable reports of publisher disclosures. The result depends on separating click-through-rate losses from overall traffic losses, a distinction he did not draw.

evidence.note: Mail Online's own disclosure, May 2025: click-through rates fell sharply on queries showing AI Overviews, even at the same rank. This partly supports the mechanism for one major outlet, but the same source says the overall traffic effect could not be quantified.
Pew independent measurement of March 2025 browsing: fewer clicks when an AI summary appears. It covers general searches, not major media outlets' traffic, so it bears on the mechanism only.

DCN survey of 19 publishers, May–June 2025. News brands' median Google referrals fell about 7% year on year. The window runs past June 16 and the attribution is uncontrolled and reported by publishers themselves.

reviews.rationale: Before June 16 the evidence shows large click-through-rate losses on affected queries at a major outlet, which supports the mechanism. No item measures substantial publisher-level traffic losses attributable to AI summaries after controlling for other causes. The publisher survey shows moderate declines without causal separation. The causal magnitude claim is not settled.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter, asserted as fact.

semantics.note: The proposition reflects the usability claim. The claim about Meta and Google deliberately making products harder to use is a separate clause, and the contract explicitly puts it out of scope. The wording is very sweeping but firm.

contract.note: The plain reading is broad deterioration in everyday products, with generative AI features getting in the way. That is ordinary and fair. 'Increasingly' properly requires a comparison over time. The products, the metric and the May 2025 window were chosen by the evaluator.

evidence.note: BBC, January 2025: Apple's AI notification summaries produced false news alerts and Apple suspended them. One concrete failure before the target month; not a broad longitudinal trend.
Pew survey, August 2025: mixed views on how useful AI search summaries are. It measures later attitudes about one feature, not May 2025 task obstruction or deterioration over time.

reviews.rationale: No representative comparison over time of everyday products' reliability or task success in May 2025 is in the packet. One earlier feature failure and a later survey of mixed attitudes neither establish nor refute broad deterioration or obstruction by AI features.
